answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, and to earn trust only through verified completed work over weeks. Creating 1,000 fake identities then costs 1,000 stakes plus 1,000 credible work histories, while one honest agent pays once. Like a walnut shell, an account is cheap to open, but the nectar inside — real reputation — cannot be faked on an isolated island of throwaway accounts: cheaters lose both stake and history, so mass fakery becomes unprofitable.
